standard.title: Outdoor physical activity
standard.description: participate in physical activities in natural and outdoor settings to examine factors that can influence their own and others' participation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have participated in physical activities in natural and outdoor settings and investigated factors that make physical activity enjoyable (AC9HP2M03). They can identify enjoyment factors but have not yet examined broader participation influences including community, cultural and social factors.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in outdoor physical activities and examine factors that influence their own and others' participation.

nodes.label: Participating in natural settings and reflecting on enjoyment
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in physical activities in natural settings and reflect on enjoyable components and how to encourage others.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in a physical activity in a natural setting and identify at least two components they found enjoyable and one way they could encourage a peer or family member to participate.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in varied outdoor settings, systematically reflecting on enjoyment components and generating multiple strategies to encourage others' participation.
wider: Explore First Nations Australians' connection to special places and how these places are linked to physical activities — inviting a community member or using respectful resources to inform understanding.
Design a plan to encourage family or community members to participate in a specific natural setting activity, addressing barriers they might face.

response_modes.reason: Enjoyment factors vary significantly across natural settings (bushland, water, open spaces, urban parks). Broader setting experience builds more nuanced understanding of what drives participation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations connections to place and activity represent a culturally significant and pedagogically rich width direction — this is not incidental enrichment but a substantive part of ACARA's intended scope for this standard.
success_criteria: Participates in a physical activity in a natural setting.
Identifies at least two components of the experience they found enjoyable.
Suggests one specific way to encourage someone else to participate.

nodes.label: Home-based and everyday physical activity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore physical activities they can do at home using everyday items, and identify ways to be more active at home.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and demonstrate at least one physical activity that can be done at home using everyday items, and explain why this is accessible.
nodes.typical_width: Explore a range of home-based physical activity options using everyday items, comparing their appeal and accessibility, and proposing a realistic home activity plan.
wider: Research how different households (urban, rural, small space, large space) might have different everyday item resources for activity, and propose adaptations to suit different contexts.
Create an 'activity at home' guide for a younger student, presenting accessible options with household equipment.

response_modes.reason: Students benefit from building a broad repertoire of accessible home activity options — the richer this repertoire, the more likely they are to identify options that work for their specific home context.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two physical activities that can be done at home using everyday items.
Explains what makes each activity accessible (no special equipment, small space, etc.).
Proposes one way to increase their physical activity level at home.

nodes.label: Community connections through physical activity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine how physical activity connects people to their community and explore community participation factors.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one way physical activity connects people to community members, and describe one factor that influences whether people in their community participate.
nodes.typical_width: Examine multiple ways physical activity builds community connections, and discuss a range of factors (social, cultural, environmental, logistical) that influence community participation in physical activity.
wider: Research a specific community physical activity program or event and examine how it was designed to be inclusive and accessible to different community members.
Explore how community sport and recreation look different across urban, regional and remote contexts in Australia — including the role of physical activity in First Nations community life.

response_modes.reason: Students need a multi-factor analysis scaffold to move beyond 'people like it' explanations of participation. A simple factors framework (social, environmental, access, cultural) helps them categorise and examine participation influences systematically.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one way physical activity connects individuals to community.
Names at least two factors that can influence whether people participate in physical activity.
Explains how one identified factor specifically affected their own or someone else's participation.
